summary: Replaced the `beforeRegisterNodeDef` + `chainCallback(prototype,'onNodeCreated')` registration with `comfy.defs.extend('FastPreview', b => ...)`. The whole frame-correlation apparatus — the module-level `execId`, the unfiltered `executing` listener, the `b_preview_with_metadata`/`b_preview` `addEventListener` pair, the `serverSupportsFeature('supports_preview_metadata')` probe and the matching `removeEventListener` cleanup — is deleted in favour of `b.onPreview`, which delivers frames already correlated to the owning node. `node.imgs = [img]` + `setDirtyCanvas` became a `node.widgets.canvas({ draw })` surface plus `redraw()`; `setSize([550,550])` became `setSize({width,height})`. Per-node state moved to a Map keyed by node.id, cleared in `b.onRemoved`.

test:
equivalence: A FastPreview node is created at 550x550 and, when a preview frame arrives that is addressed to that node, the frame's image is rendered on the node. Passes on both the original (b_preview_with_metadata whose displayNodeId matches the node id -> node.imgs = [img], setDirtyCanvas) and the converted source (b.onPreview -> state.img set, canvas widget redrawn). Also: after the node is removed, a subsequent preview frame for that id renders nothing and leaks no listener.

fix: With TWO FastPreview nodes previewing in the same run on a server that does NOT advertise supports_preview_metadata, a plain `b_preview` frame is attributed to exactly one node — the one the backend is executing. On the ORIGINAL this fails: every FastPreview instance registers its own global `b_preview` listener and each compares the single module-level `execId` against its own id, so the frame is shown on whichever node id happens to equal execId while the other node's stale image is left in place; worse, because `execId` is module-global and updated by an unfiltered "executing" listener, a frame emitted after execId has advanced is mis-attributed to the newly-executing node even if the frame belongs to the previous one. On the CONVERTED source b.onPreview delivers the frame already correlated to the owning node, so attribution is per-node and cannot be raced by a shared global.
